claims.text: The intervention increases Mo content from x = 0.2 to x = 1 in the CoCrFeNiMox composite.
Increasing Mo to x = 1 promotes robust high-temperature oxide/molybdate glaze formation.
Increasing Mo to x = 1 promotes Mo-induced tetragonal sigma-phase formation.
The glaze and sigma-phase strengthening reduce wear and maintain low friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Higher Mo content induces significant distortion of the FCC lattice.
The Mo-rich sigma phase is hard.
High-temperature oxidation and tribochemical reactions produce a continuous interfacial glaze containing silver molybdates and NiO.
Dissolved Mo strengthens the matrix by solid-solution strengthening.
The sigma phase provides second-phase strengthening that resists plastic deformation and scratching.
At lower temperatures, MoS2 and Ag provide low-shear lubrication.
At higher temperatures, a dense oxide/molybdate glaze decreases interfacial shear stress and material removal.
Relative to Mo0.2, Mo1 will have greater hardness and wear resistance across the full tested temperature range.
At 800 °C, Mo1 will form a particularly effective glaze and exhibit lower wear while retaining comparably low friction.
Friction reduction at 200–400 °C may be less pronounced because of thermal softening and discontinuity of the lubricant film.
The Mo0.2 baseline primarily forms an FCC solid solution with little sigma phase.
The Mo0.2 baseline has a friction coefficient of approximately 0.66 at room temperature.
The Mo0.2 baseline friction coefficient peaks at approximately 0.75 at 200 °C and falls to approximately 0.21 at 800 °C.
The Mo0.2 baseline reaches a wear-rate maximum of 98.1 × 10^-6 mm³/(N·m) at 400 °C and has a lower wear rate at 800 °C.
The proposed operating boundary is dry sliding in air against Si3N4 from room temperature to 800 °C at 8 N, 0.15 m/s, and 270 m.
Performance may differ in environments other than air or under different loads.
